context: Tests first per failing sequence. Policy decisions to make explicit in the PR: extra tunings become errors (or a documented, config-gated acceptance); persist constraint enablement and per-column sort attributes in the metadata payload with a schema-version bump AND a read path that branches on version so pre-existing DBs get a clear 'metadata too old to validate strictly' outcome instead of false drift; notuning runs that find tuning metadata in a reused DB must at minimum surface a bundle-visible drift_check (decide warn-vs-refuse and document). Keep the manager connected to the connection under validation, or document why platform_config is guaranteed equivalent.
description:
From the 2026-07-31 adversarial review of benchbox/core/tuning/metadata.py (982 lines) and platforms/base/validation.py. Four defects with concrete failing sequences, all of the form 'reused DB accepted although its physical tuning differs from what the run's bundle claims':

M1 (extra tunings pass): metadata.py:805-812 - missing tables are errors but extra tables only add_warning; is_valid stays True and connection_lifecycle.py:246-258 reuses on is_valid. Sequence: run 1 tunes lineitem+orders (metadata saved for both); run 2's config tunes only orders -> extra 'lineitem' = warning -> DB reused; the bundle's requested_config_hash and tunings_applied describe an orders-only tuning while lineitem's physical layout persists; drift_check reports is_valid:true.

M2 (PK/FK drift invisible): constraint enablement is neither persisted (column rows metadata.py:466-488; section markers cover only unique/check + platform optimizations, metadata.py:226-259) nor compared (_compare_tuning_configurations metadata.py:785-821 compares tables only; rebuilt existing side gets dataclass defaults at metadata.py:683). Sequence: run 1 with primary_keys.enabled=true; run 2 reuses with enabled=false, identical table tunings -> clean pass; a 'no-PK' labeled run executes against a PK-constrained database.

M3 (sort attribute drift invisible): persistence keeps only (table, tuning_type, name, order) (metadata.py:477-488, rebuilt with type=UNKNOWN at 716-722); comparison reduces to (name, order) tuples (metadata.py:840-843). ASC re-requested as DESC (different physical layout on platforms honoring direction) passes clean. Same for nulls_position/compression.

M4 (notuning reuse unchecked): platforms/base/validation.py:118-139 - both branches require adapter.tuning_enabled; with tuning disabled neither the drift comparison nor even the 'database contains tuning metadata' warning runs. A physically tuned DB is reused and published as a notuning baseline.

Compounding smells to address opportunistically: B5 marker-write failures are silent (metadata.py:280-282) and missing markers are warnings (319-326), so section drift detection can be silently absent; B6 any load exception maps to None (657-660) then reported as 'No tuning metadata found' (767-768), misattributing connectivity failures; B7 _METADATA_SCHEMA_VERSION is written but never read (169-174); TuningMetadataManager queries go through platform_config, not the connection_config under validation (186-188 vs 300,617,647).

anti_patterns.dont: Do not fix M1 by deleting the extra tunings from the reused database
anti_patterns.instead: fail validation (recreate or refuse) and record the drift in drift_check
anti_patterns.why: destructive reconciliation of a reused DB is out of scope and dangerous

anti_patterns.dont: Do not report connectivity failures as 'no tuning metadata found'
anti_patterns.instead: propagate a distinct load-error outcome into MetadataValidationResult
anti_patterns.why: it misattributes an infrastructure error as a clean state and hides real drift

anti_patterns.dont: Do not widen the persisted payload without a version branch on read
anti_patterns.instead: bump the version, branch on it when loading, and define the legacy outcome explicitly
anti_patterns.why: _METADATA_SCHEMA_VERSION is currently written and never read; changing the shape without a read path turns every pre-change DB into false drift

preserves.behavior: Existing DBs with pre-change metadata get a deterministic, explained outcome via the schema version read path - not spurious drift errors.
Fail-closed direction on validation errors: unreadable/ambiguous metadata leads to recreate-or-refuse, never silent reuse.
Metadata persistence failure stays non-fatal to the run (tuning_metadata_saved flag semantics unchanged).
drift_check remains descriptive in the .applied.json companion and can never be a source of applied_verified (ADR-001 addendum).

verifications.description: Metadata/drift unit suites green including the four new failing-sequence tests
